A buyer came from Ikorodu, haggled for one hour twenty minutes, paid in a black nylon bag; father counted the money standing up in the sun.

facts.what_happened: Speaker worked nights on a medical ward during clinical placement because fewer students were on nights.
Patient in bed seven was named Mama Ronke.
Mama Ronke was 68, had a CVA with dense hemiplegia, was mostly aphasic, could say about three words, one of which was 'water.'
Her son and family brought her in, paid the deposit, and completed the investigations.
There is no NHIS for most people; payment is cash; once the bill passed a certain point, the family stopped coming.
Nineteen days passed.

Relatives of other patients buy drugs and diapers and pressure nurses; speaker states this pressure results in more attention.
Mama Ronke had no one advocating/pressuring on her behalf.
Speaker performed mouth care on Mama Ronke.
Speaker did this every night.
Mouth care involved using a swab and glycerine to clean the tongue and palate.
Speaker turned Mama Ronke two-hourly with help from whoever was available.
Speaker plaited Mama Ronke's hair one night because it was matting.
Speaker talked to Mama Ronke, including about a pharmacology test.
Mama Ronke looked at the ceiling.
Sister Adaeze told the speaker, 'Temi, you're doing too much, this is not your patient alone, you have six others.'
Speaker responded, 'yes ma.'
Speaker did not stop the extra care.
Mama Ronke died on a Thursday, about ten to five in the morning.
Speaker was present at the time of death.
The breathing changed and then stopped; described as not dramatic.
Sister Adaeze guided the speaker through last offices.
Last offices procedure included washing the body, positioning it, packing with cotton wool, removing the cannula and catheter, identification, writing the tag, and recording the time on the chart.
During the procedure, speaker's hands were steady and mind was clear; afterward went to the changing room and sat on the bench.
Mama Ronke's small black comb is in the speaker's bag.
The comb has been in the bag since last year.
The son came on Friday.
He was crying.
Speaker took him to the office, gave him water, and told him she was comfortable.
Son said, 'thank you nurse, God bless you.'
Speaker said, 'it's okay sir.'
Speaker remembers the date the son last visited before that and the sound of his shoes.
